findings.requirement_type: Document Integrity — BOP, Umbrella, and WC PDFs Not Text-Extractable
findings.gap_description: Three of the five policies in the program are image-based scans (or OCR-broken PDFs) and could not be parsed into machine-readable text. As delivered, this means the bulk of the property/casualty program — General Liability and Property (BOP), the Umbrella that sits over GL/Auto/EL, and the entire Workers' Compensation policy — has not been auditable from these documents. Any RMF finding below tied to BOP, Umbrella, or WC is necessarily 'Needs Review' until OCR'd source text or carrier-issued specimen forms are available.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Cancellation Notice Below Broker Benchmark (90 days)
findings.gap_description: The Pekin Auto policy uses the standard ISO IL 00 17 cancellation terms — 10 days non-pay / 30 days other. The broker target on commercial accounts is 90 days, often achieved via a Designated Entity NOC endorsement. None is on the policy. Cancellation provisions are policy-specific and do not flow up to or down from any other policy in the program.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Unintentional Errors and Omissions Giveback
findings.gap_description: Cannot determine from extracted text whether the Pekin Commercial Auto Enhancement Endorsement (CA 31 34 10 18) includes an Unintentional Errors & Omissions giveback. Without it, an inadvertent failure to schedule a vehicle, location, or operation can give Pekin grounds to deny coverage.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Named Insured Defects (Form of Business and Individual NI Endorsement)
findings.gap_description: Two related defects on the Named Insured: (1) 'Form of Business' on the Dec is literally blank ('NOT SELECTED'), and (2) the policy carries CA 99 17 Individual Named Insured — an endorsement that extends coverage to spouse/relatives for personal autos when the Named Insured is a natural person. Precision Aero is 'Inc'. Either the policy was issued without the carrier confirming entity type (administrative defect that could surface in a misrepresentation argument at claim), or there is an undisclosed individual Named Insured (e.g., owner) for which the dec doesn't reflect. Named Insured defects on the Auto policy do not get fixed by any other policy — each policy stands on its own dec.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Notice and Knowledge of Occurrence Not Endorsed
findings.gap_description: Without a notice-and-knowledge endorsement that limits the duty to report to a designated officer / risk manager / person responsible for insurance, any driver-employee's knowledge of a fender-bender or near-miss is technically imputed to Precision Aero. If reporting is delayed because a low-level driver didn't escalate, Pekin can argue late notice and reduce or deny coverage. Notice provisions are policy-specific; not addressable by another policy in the program.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Waiver of Subrogation (Blanket)
findings.gap_description: Cannot determine from extracted text whether blanket Waiver of Subrogation is provided. Most customer contracts and lease agreements require WoS where permitted by law. If CA 31 34 does not include a blanket WoS giveback, every WoS request will require a manuscript endorsement on a per-contract basis.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Additional Insured: Automatic + WoS + Primary & Non-Contributory
findings.gap_description: Cannot confirm automatic Additional Insured status, blanket Waiver of Subrogation, or Primary & Non-Contributory wording on the Auto policy without reading CA 31 34. These are routine contract requirements (lease agreements, customer contracts, vendor agreements).

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Bodily Injury Definition Includes Mental Anguish
findings.gap_description: Standalone mental anguish coverage (mental anguish unaccompanied by physical injury) is often excluded from BI under the unmodified ISO definition. Cannot confirm whether the Pekin enhancement endorsement broadens BI to include mental anguish independent of physical injury.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Broad Named Insured Endorsement Not Present
findings.gap_description: If Precision Aero has any related entities — holding company, real estate LLC for the 5310 S 32nd St property, ESOP/profit-sharing trust, sister company, JV — none of them are named on this Auto policy. A broad form NI endorsement that automatically extends coverage to subsidiaries (and often majority-controlled affiliates) is the standard fix, but it's not on this policy. Named Insured definitions are policy-specific; even if the BOP/WC/Umbrella have broad NI wording (cannot verify, those PDFs are not text-extractable), each policy still requires its own NI structure for its own coverage.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Lease Gap Coverage
findings.gap_description: N/A — no leased vehicles on the schedule. Lease Gap coverage is therefore not currently needed.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Drive Other Car Endorsement
findings.gap_description: Drive Other Car (DOC) extends company auto liability/UM/UIM/Med Pay to a designated executive officer when driving a non-owned vehicle in which they have no other coverage (e.g., they don't carry personal auto). Without it, an exec officer who drives a borrowed or rented car in their personal capacity has no coverage from the corporate policy — and may have nothing personal because they don't own a car.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Employee as Insured (CA 9933) and Employee Hired Auto (CA 2054)
findings.gap_description: CA 99 33 makes employees insureds for liability when driving any covered auto in the employer's business (closes the 'employee driving a non-owned car on company errand' gap). CA 20 54 extends physical damage to an auto rented by an employee in the employer's name. Both are routine for businesses with employees who run errands or rent vehicles for travel.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Pollution / Environmental Endorsement (Limited Pollution CA 99 48)
findings.gap_description: Standard ISO Auto excludes pollution arising from cargo being transported and from operating equipment attached to the auto. CA 99 48 narrows the exclusion to give back coverage for upset/overturn of fluids in the operation of the auto. For a manufacturer that may transport coolants, lubricants, cutting oils, or solvents in any volume in a covered auto, the absence of CA 99 48 means a fluid spill from a tipped vehicle could be uncovered. Cannot verify whether the Umbrella or BOP backstops this — both are not text-extractable. Standard Umbrellas typically follow form on Auto pollution exclusions, so the Umbrella is unlikely to drop down. Leaving as Bad until other policies can be verified.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Fellow Employee Exclusion Deletion
findings.gap_description: By default the Auto policy excludes one employee suing another (or the company) for injuries sustained while both were acting in the course of employment in a covered auto. Some employers want this exclusion deleted so an injured employee/passenger can recover beyond Workers' Compensation; others prefer to keep it to limit cross-claim exposure. The decision depends on Precision Aero's preference and applicable state law.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Hired Auto Physical Damage NOT Purchased
findings.gap_description: Hired Auto Liability is in place, but Hired Auto Physical Damage (Comp and Collision) was not purchased. If Precision Aero rents a truck, van, or trailer for any reason and that rental is damaged in a collision, hits a deer, is stolen, or is damaged by hail, Pekin will not pay for the damage to the rental vehicle. Rental agreements universally make the renter responsible for physical damage. Personal credit-card coverage rarely extends to commercial rentals or trucks. Loss-of-use charges from the rental agency would also fall on Precision Aero. This is a first-party physical damage gap; no other policy in the program (BOP property, Umbrella, EPLI, WC) covers damage to a hired auto. The BOP property form would not extend to a vehicle rented and operated on the road. Confirmed Ugly.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Hired Auto Cost-of-Hire Estimate ($1,000/yr)
findings.gap_description: The Hired Auto premium is rated against an estimated annual cost of hire of $1,000. If Precision Aero's actual rental spend exceeds this materially, premium audit will result in additional billing AND a creative carrier could argue at claim that the unreported rental activity creates a coverage dispute. Premium-rating issues are policy-specific.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Symbol 7 Limitation on Phys Damage / UM / UIM / Med Pay
findings.gap_description: Liability uses Symbol 1 (Any Auto) — correct. But Med Pay, UM, UIM, and Phys Damage all use Symbol 7 (Specifically Described Autos) — meaning only the 2018 Ram and 2020 Express are covered for those coverages. Any other vehicle the business operates — a newly acquired truck before it's added, a rented vehicle, a borrowed vehicle, an employee's personal vehicle on company business — has no Med Pay, no UM, no UIM, and no Phys Damage protection from this policy. Umbrellas typically do not drop down on first-party Med Pay / UM / UIM / Phys Damage; these are coverage-specific to the underlying Auto. No backstop from another policy.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Limits Match Liability
findings.gap_description: UM and UIM limits match the $1M liability limit. This is the recommended structure — anything less leaves your own employees with less protection (when an at-fault uninsured driver hits them) than you'd give a third party they hurt.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Uninsured Motorist Property Damage (UMPD) Not Purchased
findings.gap_description: UMPD is optional in Arizona. Without it, when an uninsured driver damages a Precision Aero vehicle, the only path to repair is through Collision (Symbol 7), subject to a $500 deductible. Many AZ insureds buy UMPD specifically to avoid using their own deductible after an uninsured-driver loss. UMPD is auto-specific and not covered by any other policy in the program.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Motor Truck Cargo / In-Transit Coverage Not Purchased
findings.covered_by_which_policy: Possibly the BOP — cannot verify until OCR'd. Possibly missing entirely — no Inland Marine policy was provided.
findings.gap_description: No cargo coverage in this Auto policy. For a machine shop / aerospace manufacturer transporting precision-machined parts, raw stock, tooling, or finished components in their own vehicles, an accident that damages the cargo has no coverage under Auto. Whether this is a real exposure depends on what Precision Aero actually moves in their two trucks. May be picked up under the BOP's Property in Transit sublimit (cannot verify — BOP not text-extractable) or by an Inland Marine policy if one exists (none was provided in this audit). Leaving as Bad with verification flag.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Mobile Equipment vs Auto Definition
findings.gap_description: The Auto policy and the GL/BOP each have a definition of 'mobile equipment' vs 'auto.' A piece of equipment that is legally classified as an 'auto' (e.g., a road-licensed yard tractor) needs to be on the Auto policy; equipment that's truly mobile equipment falls under GL. Misclassification can leave gaps.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Vehicle Ownership / Lease Documentation
findings.gap_description: If either vehicle is titled in the name of an owner, an LLC, or another entity instead of Precision Aero Inc, the named insured doesn't have insurable interest as expected and we may need either to add the title-holder as Additional Named Insured / Additional Insured or to use CA 99 47 (Employee as Lessor).

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Temporary & Leased Workers Exclusion from Employee Definition
findings.gap_description: If Precision Aero uses staffing agencies / leased workers / temporary employees who drive on company business, those workers may end up classified as 'employees' under the Auto policy — making them insureds for liability and triggering the Fellow Employee exclusion (which prevents them from suing). Whether Precision Aero wants this depends on their risk philosophy. The staffing agency's policy should typically be the one to respond if a leased worker drives on the company's behalf.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — No-Fault State Coverages
findings.gap_description: N/A — Arizona is not a no-fault state. Personal Injury Protection (PIP) and no-fault medical / wage / death benefits are not required.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Parked Vehicles / Aggregate Deductible
findings.gap_description: N/A — only two vehicles. Aggregate deductible structures are typically only useful for fleet operations where multiple parked vehicles could be damaged in one event (hail, fire, wind).

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Page Integrity Anomaly (CU Umbrella Page Misbound)
findings.gap_description: Pages 21–22 of the Auto PDF appear to belong to a different policy (likely the Pekin Umbrella, policy 005935979). They are misbound into the Auto file. This is a documentation defect — not a coverage defect — but it creates ambiguity if a third party (court, other carrier, certificate holder) ever reviews the policy.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Carrier Broadening Endorsement Text Not Provided (CA 31 34)
findings.gap_description: Pekin's Commercial Auto Enhancement Endorsement (CA 31 34) is the proprietary broadening package for the policy. It typically contains automatic Additional Insured status, blanket Waiver of Subrogation, Hired Auto Physical Damage giveback, Drive Other Car, Employee Hired Auto, expanded Mental Anguish, and similar broadenings. Without the form text, the audit cannot conclude on any of those items — they appear as 'Needs Review' in findings 6, 7, 8, 11, 12 above.

findings.requirement_type: Auto — Asbestos / Lead / Silica / Hydraulic Fracturing Exclusions
findings.gap_description: These are carrier-standard pollution-style exclusions on the Auto policy. None apply to typical machine-shop auto operations (silica is a real GL exposure at the shop floor, but not from operating a truck). Acceptable on Auto.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Cancellation Notice Not Visible on Renewal Certificate
findings.gap_description: Cannot determine cancellation notice period from the renewal certificate alone. AZ statute typically requires at least 10 days for non-pay and longer for non-renewal. Whether USLI has additional broadening to meet the 90-day broker benchmark is unknown.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Named Insured Verification
findings.gap_description: If Precision Aero has any related entities (holding co, real-estate LLC, ESOP trust, sister companies) that share employees or could be sued in an employment matter, those entities are not insured under this EPLI policy. Same gap as on Auto (finding-009) — needs the same org-chart review.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Notice and Knowledge / Claim Reporting Provisions
findings.gap_description: EPLI is claims-made — late reporting can void coverage. EPL-169 modifies the standard notice provisions; whether it tightens or loosens the trigger is unknown without the form text. Knowledge typically must be limited to the person responsible for insurance to avoid imputed knowledge from a low-level supervisor.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Limit Inadequate for a Manufacturer ($1M Aggregate)
findings.gap_description: $1M aggregate is the same-and-only bucket for every claim during the policy year. A single discrimination, harassment, or wrongful-termination class action can consume $1M in defense costs alone, especially if regulatory agencies (EEOC, AZ Civil Rights Division) get involved or claimants are multiple. With defense likely inside the limit (must verify against EPL-J base form), one moderately serious matter could exhaust the aggregate, leaving zero coverage for the rest of the policy year. Standard commercial Umbrellas typically do NOT schedule EPLI as underlying coverage and do NOT extend over EPLI; absent verification that the Pekin Umbrella schedules USLI EPL1575392A as underlying (Umbrella PDF not text-extractable), no excess relief should be assumed.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Retroactive Date Limits Prior Acts to 1 Year
findings.gap_description: Policy inception was 11/30/2023 with retro date 11/30/2022 — only 1 year of prior acts. Employment claims commonly arise long after the underlying conduct (a 2021 termination resulting in a 2024 EEOC charge would be uncovered). If Precision Aero had EPLI in prior years (continuous coverage), the retro date should match the earliest continuous EPLI inception date, not be limited to 1 year. Retro-date defects are EPLI-specific and not curable by any other policy in the program.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Biometric Information Exclusion (Manufacturer Exposure)
findings.gap_description: If Precision Aero uses biometric employee identification — fingerprint or hand-scan time clocks, facial recognition for plant access, retina scans — this exclusion creates a complete coverage gap. Biometric privacy class actions under Illinois BIPA, Texas CUBI, and California CCPA-style statutes have produced single-employer settlements exceeding $50M. Arizona doesn't have a BIPA-equivalent yet but federal and other-state class actions are still possible if any employee or plant visitor is from one of those jurisdictions. No other policy in the program (no Cyber, no D&O) is likely to respond. The BOP CGL almost certainly has its own data privacy / personal-and-advertising-injury exclusions; the Umbrella would follow form on EPLI exclusions. Confirmed Ugly.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Wage & Hour (FLSA) Sublimit
findings.gap_description: Wage & hour is the highest-frequency, highest-severity employment exposure in most jurisdictions. EPL-162 sublimits FLSA / state wage-law claims rather than giving them the full $1M aggregate. Sublimit dollar amount must be confirmed against the form text. If sublimit is below $250K defense for a manufacturer with hourly workers, this is materially inadequate. Wage-and-hour exposure is exclusively an EPLI line; no other policy in the program addresses it.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Defense Costs Erode Retention
findings.gap_description: Standard EPLI structure — insured pays first $25K of defense costs before USLI dollars engage. This is normal. Worth flagging in plain English so Precision Aero knows what to budget.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Defense Inside vs Outside Limit (EPL-167 Loss Definition)
findings.gap_description: Most EPLI forms have defense costs INSIDE the policy limit — meaning legal fees erode the $1M. EPL-167 amends the definition of Loss; the amendment may further narrow what's covered (e.g., punitive damages, front pay, back pay, liquidated damages may be carved out). All this requires reading the form.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Third-Party Harassment Coverage
findings.gap_description: Third-party EPLI extends coverage to claims of harassment or discrimination brought by non-employees (customers, vendors, visitors). Many EPLI forms include third-party automatically; some require an endorsement.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Definition of Employee (Temps, 1099, Leased)
findings.gap_description: Whether 'Employee' under the EPLI includes temps, leased workers, and 1099 contractors materially affects who can bring a claim against the policy and who is excluded. For a manufacturer that may use staffing agencies during production peaks, this matters.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Carrier Strength (USLI / Berkshire Hathaway, A++)
findings.gap_description: Top-tier carrier. No financial-strength concern.

findings.requirement_type: EPLI — Renewal Certificate Only / Full Policy Required
findings.policy_page: Pg. 8 endorsement schedule references all forms; only EPL-148 retro endorsement text is in the file (Pg. 11)
findings.gap_description: Multiple EPLI findings above are 'Needs Review' for the same root cause: only the renewal certificate was provided, not the full policy. Pulling the complete policy resolves findings 29, 31, 35, 37, 38, 39 in one move.

findings.requirement_type: BOP — Full Audit Pending OCR (All RMF Items)
findings.gap_description: The BOP is the General Liability + Property anchor of the program. Until the document is OCR'd or replaced with a native-text PDF, NONE of the CGL RMF items (Additional Insured, Waiver of Subrogation, Primary & Non-Contributory, Contractual Liability, Per-Project / Per-Location Aggregate, Damage to Premises Rented, Mental Anguish in BI, Care/Custody/Control, Total Pollution Exclusion, Hired & Non-Owned, EBL, Stop Gap, Faulty Work giveback, Fellow Employee, Notice & Knowledge, TRIA, etc.) can be evaluated. Same applies to all 5 General All Policies items for the BOP.

findings.requirement_type: Umbrella — Full Audit Pending OCR (All RMF Items)
findings.gap_description: All 14 Umbrella RMF items (Endorsements list, non-follow-form exclusions, horizontal exhaustion / WoS follow-form, Insureds AI/NI follow-form, defense inside vs outside limits, maintenance of underlying, Notice & Knowledge, per-project aggregate follow-form, Professional Liability, Punitive Damages exclusion, Right & Duty when underlying exhausted, Total Pollution Exclusion, Schedule of Underlying, specific follow-form concerns) plus 5 General All Policies items cannot be evaluated. The CU 21 44 page that strayed into the Auto PDF suggests the Umbrella has a Conditional Terrorism Exclusion — meaningful but only indicative.

findings.requirement_type: Workers' Comp — Full Audit Pending OCR (All RMF Items)
findings.gap_description: All 15 substantive WC RMF items (small indemnity claims management / back-to-work, small medical claims, All States Endorsement Item 3.A vs 3.C, Alternate Employer endorsement on staffing-firm policy, EL limits sufficiency for Umbrella, Foreign Voluntary / Endemic Disease / Repatriation, Experience Modification trend, Maritime, Large claims management, premium credits, Owners Excluded, DBA, USL&H/MEL, classification codes correct, Waiver of Subrogation) plus 5 General All Policies items cannot be evaluated.

findings.requirement_type: Program Gap — No Cyber/Privacy Liability Policy
findings.gap_description: A precision aero / machine shop manufacturer holds: (a) customer drawings and CAD files often subject to ITAR or EAR controls, (b) personally identifiable information of employees, (c) bank credentials used for ACH/wire payments to suppliers, (d) network-connected CNC machinery susceptible to ransomware. None of these exposures are covered by Auto, EPLI, GL (the BOP almost certainly excludes cyber via CG 21 06 / similar), Umbrella, or WC. The biometric privacy exposure is also uncovered (see finding-034). Average ransomware cost to a US manufacturer in 2024 was over $5M including recovery, business interruption, and ransom. A single phishing-driven wire fraud loss commonly runs $100K–$500K. Confirmed Ugly — coverage absent program-wide.

findings.requirement_type: Program Gap — No D&O / Directors & Officers Policy
findings.gap_description: Even private-company D&O matters: claims by lenders, vendors, customers, and minority shareholders against directors and officers personally are not covered by GL, EPLI, Umbrella, Auto, or WC. For a private manufacturer with bank debt, D&O typically runs $5K–$15K for $1M of coverage and protects the personal assets of owners. Coverage absent program-wide.

findings.requirement_type: Program Gap — No Crime / Fidelity Bond Disclosed
findings.gap_description: A small embedded Crime sublimit on a BOP (typically $10K–$25K Employee Theft, often $0 Computer/Funds Transfer Fraud) is rarely enough for a manufacturer with active accounts payable, payroll processing, and supplier wires. Common loss: a senior bookkeeper diverting $50K–$300K over months before discovery. Also common: phishing-driven wire fraud (Social Engineering), which is usually a separate sublimit and may be excluded entirely from a BOP. BOP not text-extractable; partial coverage may exist but cannot be verified, so leaving as Bad.

findings.requirement_type: Program Gap — No Inland Marine / Equipment / Tools Coverage Disclosed
findings.gap_description: Manufacturers commonly need: (a) Transportation/Transit coverage for finished parts moving to customers (especially relevant given finding-020 — no Cargo on Auto), (b) Property in Custody of Bailees if customers send tooling/fixtures into the shop, (c) Tools & Equipment Floater for off-premises shop tools, (d) Computers & Electronic Data Processing (often broader than BOP property's EDP sublimit). All depend on what's already in the BOP.

findings.requirement_type: Program Gap — No Product Recall / Product Withdrawal Coverage Disclosed
findings.gap_description: For an aerospace parts supplier, a defect in a critical component can trigger an FAA-driven Airworthiness Directive or customer-mandated recall. The cost of identifying affected parts, transporting them, replacing them, and customer cleanup is not covered by standard GL — only the resulting BI/PD claims are. Recall costs for an aerospace component can easily reach $250K–$1M+ per event before any liability claim is filed. Recall is a stand-alone product line; not addressed elsewhere in the program.

findings.requirement_type: Program Gap — No Professional Liability / Errors & Omissions Disclosed
findings.gap_description: Whether Precision Aero needs Manufacturer's E&O depends on operations: do they design parts to a customer's spec, or do they just machine to provided drawings? Build-to-print shops generally don't need E&O; design-build shops and shops that recommend material substitutions or process changes do. GL responds to BI/PD; E&O responds to financial loss caused by faulty work / negligent design / failure to perform.

findings.requirement_type: Program Gap — No Environmental / Pollution Liability Disclosed (CPL/PLL)
findings.gap_description: A machine shop / aerospace shop typically uses cutting fluids, hydraulic oils, solvents, plating chemistry, anodizing baths, and degreasers. A spill or release on-premises (or migrating off-premises) can trigger AZ DEQ cleanup orders. The standard CGL pollution exclusion typically blocks coverage. Premises Pollution Liability (PLL) is the answer for fixed-location risks; Contractors Pollution Liability (CPL) is for off-site work.

findings.requirement_type: Program Gap — No Foreign Liability / Foreign Voluntary WC Disclosed
findings.gap_description: If Precision Aero sells to international customers (common for aerospace suppliers via Tier 1 OEMs that ship globally), or if any employees travel internationally for sales, supplier visits, customer meetings, or trade shows, a Foreign Liability package addresses GL/Auto/WC overseas — none of which extend automatically from US policies.

findings.requirement_type: Cross-Program — Named Insured Asymmetry Across Policies
findings.gap_description: Cannot verify whether all five policies use the same Named Insured. Even minor variations ('Inc' vs ', Inc.' vs 'Incorporated') usually don't matter, but if BOP/Umbrella/WC name a different entity (e.g., a holding company, a trust, an old DBA), there's a structural problem.

findings.requirement_type: Cross-Program — Umbrella Attachment to Underlying EL / GL / Auto
findings.policy_page: Auto Pg. 19; Umbrella all pages; WC all pages
findings.gap_description: An Umbrella only attaches if the underlying policies (Auto, GL, EL) have limits at or above the Umbrella's required underlying. Auto is $1M — typical Umbrella attachment is $1M Auto, so likely OK. But EL on the WC and GL on the BOP cannot be verified. If EL is $500K on the WC but the Umbrella requires $1M EL underlying, there's a $500K gap before the Umbrella attaches.

findings.requirement_type: Cross-Program — Concentration of Pekin (Auto + WC + Umbrella)
findings.gap_description: Three of the five policies appear to be with Pekin. Concentration is operationally convenient (one renewal, one billing, one claims contact) but creates strategic risk: if Pekin non-renews, the entire program is up for re-quote in a hardening market. Also: Pekin's Umbrella sitting over Pekin's Auto and Pekin's WC means Pekin controls both the underlying decision and the excess decision in a serious claim — there is no second carrier providing an independent reservation-of-rights / coverage-position check.
